name: Automaize Restaurant Reservation
author: automaize

sections.description:
Automaize Restaurant Reservation adds a simple, self-contained table booking form to your restaurant website.

For the restaurant owner:

  • Define your weekly opening hours (per day of the week).
  • Add closed periods for holidays or vacation, which override the weekly hours for those dates.
  • Add your tables, each with its own seat count.
  • Choose which reservation lengths guests can pick from (e.g. 60, 90, 120 minutes), or turn duration selection off entirely so guests just book a table with no fixed length (it’s then held until closing time).
  • Set the email address that should receive new reservation notifications.
  • Set the sender name shown on reservation emails, instead of “WordPress”.
  • Manage and cancel reservations from a simple admin screen, optionally emailing the guest a cancellation notice with your own custom message.
  • Add reservations manually (phone bookings, walk-ins) straight from the admin screen, with the guest confirmation email optional.
  • Customize the wording of the guest confirmation and cancellation emails, with placeholders for the reservation details.
  • Look up any past guest by name or email and see their full reservation history plus special requests in one place, and keep staff-only notes about them (preferences, allergies, etc.).
  • Print a clean, ready-to-hand-to-staff daily reservations list for any date.

For your guests, on the reservation form:

  1. Enter the number of guests.
  2. Pick a date and how long they’d like to stay.
  3. See, in real time, whether a table is available for that party size and time.
  4. Enter their name, email, optionally a phone number and any special requests, and book instantly.
  5. Receive an email confirmation. The restaurant owner is notified by email as well.

The plugin matches each reservation to the smallest available table that fits the party size, so a party of two won’t tie up your largest table, and automatically prevents double-booking a table for overlapping time windows.

No external services or API keys required, and no data ever leaves your site.

AI disclosure

This plugin’s code was developed with the assistance of an AI coding tool (Claude, by Anthropic). All code was reviewed and tested by Automaize before release.

Usage

Add the reservation form to any page or post in either of these ways:

  • Shortcode: place [amzres_reservation_form] in the page/post content, in a Shortcode block, or in any widget area that supports shortcodes.
  • Elementor: drag the “Restaurant Reservation Form” widget (listed under the General category) onto the page, if Elementor is active.

Both display the exact same form; there is nothing extra to configure per placement, since opening hours, tables and durations are all set once under Reservations.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/automaize-restaurant-reservation directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen directly.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Reservations → Tables and add your tables.
  4. Go to Reservations → Settings and set your opening hours, allowed reservation durations and notification email. The shortcode is also shown on this screen.
  5. Add the [amzres_reservation_form] shortcode to a page, or add the “Restaurant Reservation Form” widget in Elementor.
sections.faq:
Can I have different opening hours per day?

Yes. Each day of the week has its own opening/closing time, and can be marked closed entirely.

Can I close the restaurant for a holiday or vacation?

Yes. Under Reservations → Settings, add a closed period with a start and end date (and an optional reason, for your own reference). Dates within that range are treated as closed regardless of the weekly opening hours.

Can I print a list of the day’s reservations for my staff?

Yes. On Reservations, pick a date next to “Print daily list for” and click Print. It opens a clean, printer-friendly page listing that day’s confirmed reservations by time, with table, party size, guest and contact details.

What happens if two guests try to book the last table at the same time?

Availability is re-checked on the server at the moment a reservation is submitted, so only one of them will succeed; the other is asked to choose a different time.

Does this plugin send confirmation emails?

Yes, it uses wp_mail() to send a confirmation to the guest and a notification to the restaurant’s configured email address. When you cancel a reservation from the admin screen, you can optionally send the guest a cancellation email with your own custom message.

Can I change the sender name shown on these emails?

Yes. Under Reservations → Settings → Email sender name, set the name shown to recipients instead of the WordPress default “WordPress”. It defaults to your site’s name.

Can I customize the wording of the confirmation and cancellation emails?

Yes. Under Reservations → Settings → Email templates, edit the subject and body of both emails. Placeholders like {guest_name}, {date}, {time} and {details} are replaced with the actual reservation details when the email is sent; leave a field blank to restore its default text.

Can I add a reservation myself, e.g. for a phone booking or walk-in?

Yes. On Reservations, click “+ Add reservation”, pick a table, date, time and the guest’s details. You can choose whether to send the guest a confirmation email; availability is still checked against existing bookings for that table.

Can I skip asking guests for a reservation length?

Yes. Under Reservations → Settings → Reservation duration, uncheck “Ask for a reservation length”. Guests then just pick a date, time and party size; the duration field disappears from the form, and each booked table is held for the rest of that day’s service (until closing time) instead of a fixed number of minutes.

Can I see a guest’s past reservations in one place?

Yes. Go to Reservations → Guests, search by name or email, and open a guest to see every reservation they’ve made (including any special requests they entered) plus a staff-only notes log where you can jot down things like preferences or allergies. Guests are matched by email address. You can also get there directly by clicking a guest’s name on the Reservations screen.

Does this require any external services or API keys?

No. Everything runs on your own WordPress installation.

Does this work with Elementor?

Yes, a native “Restaurant Reservation Form” widget is available in the Elementor editor (under the General category) whenever Elementor is active. It renders the exact same form as the [amzres_reservation_form] shortcode.

Does this work with Breakdance or other page builders?

Yes. Use the [amzres_reservation_form] shortcode in your page builder’s Shortcode or Code/HTML element (Breakdance, Divi, Bricks, etc. all provide one). The form works the same way everywhere it’s placed.
sections.changelog:
1.8.0

  • Added a Guests screen: look up any past guest by name or email and see their full reservation history (including special requests) in one place, plus a staff-only notes log for preferences, allergies, etc. Guest names on the Reservations screen now link directly to their profile.

1.7.0

  • Added a way to turn off reservation duration selection entirely: guests just pick a date, time and party size, and the table is held until closing time instead of a fixed length.

1.6.0

  • Added a way to add reservations manually from the admin screen (e.g. for phone bookings or walk-ins), with the guest confirmation email optional.
  • Added editable email templates: customize the subject and body of the guest confirmation and cancellation emails under Settings, with placeholders for the reservation details.

1.5.0

  • Added an optional cancellation email: when cancelling a reservation from the admin screen, you can now include your own custom message, or skip the email entirely.
  • Added an “Email sender name” setting so reservation emails no longer show “WordPress” as the sender.

1.4.0

  • Added a printable daily reservations list: pick a date on the Reservations screen to open a clean, print-ready page for handing to staff.

1.3.0

  • Renamed all internal function, class, hook and option names to use a unique amzres_/AMZRES_ prefix (previously arr_/ARR_, which was too short and could conflict with other plugins), per WordPress.org plugin review requirements. Existing data is migrated automatically on update; no action needed.
  • Removed the bundled German translation files. Translations for WordPress.org-hosted plugins are managed automatically via translate.wordpress.org.

1.2.0

  • Added closed periods (holidays, vacation): date ranges under Settings that override the weekly opening hours.

1.1.0

  • Added an optional “Special requests” field to the reservation form, shown to the restaurant owner in the admin reservations list and in both emails.
  • Fixed the time selector only ever showing one bookable time slot in some setups.
  • Fixed the anti-spam honeypot field being visible when the form was rendered outside the shortcode’s own page content (e.g. some page builder widgets).

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
